analysis.investment_thesis: Beezaasan is a sub-300 Cr niche explosives maker riding India's mining/infrastructure tailwind, with EBITDA compounding 55% and net profit 67% CAGR over 3 years against a P/E of just 22 — a PEG well under 0.5 on paper. But this is a freshly-listed micro-cap whose equity tripled via IPO in FY25 and whose free cash flow has been negative every year, so the "story" needs another 2-3 quarters of clean execution before sizing up.
key_strengths: Operating profit 6→23 Cr in 3 years (56% CAGR) with margins expanding from ~4% to ~11%
ROE 20.2% / ROCE 22.8% on a small base — capital is working hard
PEG ~0.3-0.5 (P/E 22 vs 50%+ earnings growth) — classic GARP setup if growth holds
key_risks: Free cash flow negative every year (-12 Cr in FY25); growth funded by IPO proceeds + debt, not internal cash
Revenue lumpy: 141→228→188→215 — not a clean compounder, suggests order/project dependence
Just-listed micro-cap with thin liquidity, limited disclosure history, and heavy CWIP (13 Cr) yet to prove ROI
red_flags: OCF (5 Cr) vastly trails reported PAT (14 Cr) in FY25 — earnings quality needs scrutiny
Revenue dipped 18% in FY24 before recovering — the growth line isn't linear
analysis.detailed_analysis: This is the kind of small-cap niche dominator I love to find — explosives is a boring, regulated business with real moats (licensing, safety track record), and India's mining/road/defence capex cycle is a visible consumer-level tailwind. The numbers are seductive: EBITDA up nearly 4x in three years, ROCE near 23%, promoter holding a confident 70.7%, and a P/E of 22 against 50%+ earnings growth gives a PEG that screams "buy" on a calculator. Market cap of 288 Cr on FY25 PAT of 14 Cr means there's real room to ten-bag if they scale to even 100 Cr revenue per quarter.
